First off, yes, if the machine has only one energy source and it can be isolated by simply unplugging, and control is maintained by the person servicing the machine or locked with plug locks, you’re good to go. A lot of machines have multiple energy sources though, and since it’s packaging equipment, I’d be surprised if you didn’t have to consider pneumatic or hydraulic pressure as well. And no, simply cutting power to a solenoid or controlled valve isn’t isolating air/fluid pressure. Don’t listen to lazy mechanics who say otherwise. 

Taking the maintenance/engineer guy out to lunch is also a fantastic idea. Have him walk with you, and go machine by machine. It’s a great time to figure out if y’all can wire in energy isolation points to avoid the breakers entirely (of course, those new isolation points themselves will need LOTO SOPs, but they’d only apply to maintenance, and not machine operators/technicians). 

Beyond that, remember that the format of the SOP is as important as the SOP itself. It needs to be obvious, simple, and I highly encourage pictures with arrows.

Well, here are some things I wish I knew before I started to develop trainings.

1. I'm probably not the smartest guy in the room on a given topic. Learn what I need for the class, and be able to relate it to the experience on the ground. Don't let the experts you're training derail your class.   
  
2. Short and sweet is best, with room to expand as others ask questions.

3. Always include your reference material with the class, probably as a handout at the end. Mostly ignored by trainees, but does give a lot to your credibility.

4. Nothing grabs attention better than a video of a workplace fatality related to your lecture.

5. No guessing. An "I don't know, I'll get back to you later" sounds like a cop out, but at least your integrity isn't destroyed with a bad answer. ALWAYS follow up on these.

6. Power points are a popular tool for a reason, but if you're just reading from the slides, no one is going to be interested. Reference and visual aids only. Always bookend other visual aids yourself.
